history: Kartódromo Internacional da Granja Viana, located in Cotia, near São Paulo, Brazil, has been a cornerstone of Brazilian karting since its opening in 1996. It quickly became a hub for both amateur and professional karters, hosting numerous national and international events. While the full circuit configuration is arguably the most well-known, the Short Circuit layout, with its tighter and more technical nature, has played a crucial role in developing driver skills and providing thrilling racing action. The venue's commitment to karting is evident in its constant upgrades and its central role in the Brazilian motorsport scene, nurturing future talent that often progresses to Formula racing.
atmosphere: Standing trackside at Granja Viana during a Short Circuit race is an assault on the senses. The high-pitched whine of two-stroke engines fills the air, punctuated by the squeal of tires as karts navigate the tight corners. The crowd, a mix of passionate fans, supportive families, and aspiring drivers, buzzes with anticipation. The smell of burning rubber and high-octane fuel hangs heavy in the air, a testament to the intense competition unfolding on the track. Every corner is a battle, and the close proximity of the barriers and the other karts creates a palpable sense of danger and excitement.
trackCharacter: The Short Circuit layout at Granja Viana is a demanding test of karting prowess. Its reduced length and increased number of tight corners compared to the full circuit places a premium on precise kart control, braking finesse, and quick reflexes. Flow is sacrificed for a stop-start rhythm, rewarding drivers who can maximize acceleration out of the slow corners and maintain momentum through the technical sections. Overtaking is challenging but not impossible, often requiring bold moves and strategic positioning. This layout favors nimble karts and adaptable drivers.

famousCorners.name: Curva do Café
famousCorners.description: A fast, sweeping right-hander that requires commitment and precision to carry maximum speed through.
famousCorners.challenge: Maintaining the optimal line and carrying enough speed without running wide and losing momentum.

famousCorners.name: Retão
famousCorners.description: Despite its name meaning 'straight,' it's a short run but crucial for setting up overtakes into the Senna 'S'.
famousCorners.challenge: Maximizing exit speed from the preceding corner to gain an advantage down the straight.

famousCorners.name: Curva 6
famousCorners.description: A tight hairpin that demands a late braking maneuver.
famousCorners.challenge: Nailing the braking point to avoid overshooting the corner while maintaining enough speed to carry through.

famousCorners.name: Curva do Lago
famousCorners.description: A slightly banked left-hander that requires a delicate balance of throttle and steering.
famousCorners.challenge: Finding the right balance between corner speed and stability to maintain momentum and avoid scrubbing speed.

weatherNotes: The weather at Granja Viana is typically warm and humid, with occasional rain showers, especially during the summer months (December to February). Rain can dramatically alter the track conditions, making the surface slippery and increasing the importance of tire management and kart setup. The high humidity can also affect engine performance, requiring adjustments to the carburetor settings.
drivingAdvice: On the Short Circuit at Granja Viana, patience and precision are key. Focus on nailing your braking points and maximizing your corner exit speed, as these are the areas where you can gain the most time. Be aggressive but smart with your overtaking, and don't be afraid to use the kart's weight to your advantage in the tighter corners. Tire management is also crucial, especially in longer races, so try to avoid excessive wheelspin and sliding.
famousRaces: Various rounds of the Brazilian Karting Championship are regularly held on different Granja Viana layouts, including the Short Circuit, showcasing Brazil's top karting talent.
The 500 Milhas de Kart: While typically run on the full circuit, shorter versions of this endurance race sometimes utilize modified layouts incorporating sections of the Short Circuit.
Regional karting events: The Short Circuit is frequently used for regional championships, providing a competitive environment for local karters.
localCulture: Cotia, where Granja Viana is located, offers a blend of urban and rural life. The local cuisine features traditional Brazilian dishes, with churrascarias (barbecue restaurants) being a popular choice. The paddock atmosphere is lively and friendly, with a strong sense of community among karters and their families. The area is also known for its vibrant arts and crafts scene, with local artisans selling their wares at nearby markets.
